recent_posts.title: Agentic CI with Buildkite: Three practical examples
recent_posts.summary: Buildkite introduces agentic workflow components that integrate AI agents into CI/CD pipelines. Three practical examples demonstrate how to use these components: a GitHub PR code review bot that analyzes pull requests and posts reviews, an automated build fixer that diagnoses failed builds and creates fix PRs, and a Linear issue handler that analyzes issues and generates implementation PRs for simpler tasks. Each example uses Claude Code with the Buildkite MCP server, model providers, pipeline triggers, and the Buildkite SDK to create flexible, adaptive workflows that respond to external events from GitHub and Linear.

recent_posts.title: Designing log-navigation tools in the Buildkite MCP server
recent_posts.summary: Buildkite developed an MCP server that helps AI agents analyze CI/CD build logs more effectively. The team discovered that raw terminal streams with ANSI codes overwhelmed LLMs, causing them to fixate on early errors rather than root causes. They solved this by preprocessing logs into Parquet format with structured entries (timestamp, content, group, flags) and creating four navigation tools: tail_logs, search_logs, read_logs, and get_logs_info. Using Claude to critique its own debugging attempts, they iteratively refined the toolset to mirror human debugging workflows, making correct analysis paths the easiest for agents to follow.

recent_posts.title: What AI is teaching us about CI
recent_posts.summary: AI coding tools are creating unprecedented scale challenges for CI/CD systems, with 90% of developers now using AI according to the 2025 DORA report. Platform teams are experiencing bottlenecks as AI-generated pull requests flood merge queues and CI throughput becomes a critical constraint even for smaller teams. Five key requirements emerge for modern CI systems: scalability to handle machine-paced development, composability to support diverse AI workflows, adaptability for dynamic pipeline execution, programmability in general-purpose languages, and governability to maintain control and prioritization. Buildkite addresses these needs with new agentic workflow components including MCP server integration, model provider connections, universal pipeline triggers, SDK support for dynamic pipelines, and AI-powered plugins for build analysis.

recent_posts.title: Changelog roundup: October '25
recent_posts.summary: Buildkite's October 2025 updates introduce Test Engine workflows for automated test management and labeling, GitHub merge queue integration for Pipelines, direct YAML secrets integration with policy-based access control, team-based permissions for block and input steps, NuGet registry support for .NET packages, Google Cloud Storage integration for Private Storage Link, and webhook notifications for package creation events. Additional improvements include HTML artifact rendering, Xcode 26 support for macOS hosted agents, and enhanced filtering capabilities across the platform.

recent_posts.title: Kubernetes with Buildkite: faster, simpler, and ready for scale
recent_posts.summary: Buildkite has updated its Kubernetes Agent Stack with simplified installation requiring only a single agent token instead of multiple configuration parameters, improved scaling to handle tens of thousands of concurrent jobs with 80% smaller Kubernetes objects, better error surfacing with full YAML specs and stack-level failure signals, out-of-the-box Prometheus integration for instant observability dashboards, and expanded Helm configuration options. Future improvements include custom scheduling policies, more granular job states, and fine-grained job configuration controls.

recent_posts.title: Post-incident review for 20th October 2025
recent_posts.summary: Buildkite experienced service degradation on October 20th, 2025, due to an AWS us-east-1 outage that prevented autoscaling during peak traffic hours. Customers faced varying degrees of latency (1.5-7 seconds average) and error rates up to 10% across web interfaces, APIs, job dispatch, and notifications between 13:00-20:36 UTC. The incident team paused deployments, shifted load between shards, and prioritized capacity increases once AWS partially restored provisioning capabilities. The company is now investigating multi-region resilience strategies and backup communication channels.

recent_posts.title: Make it work, make it better: What's new with the Buildkite MCP server
recent_posts.summary: Buildkite released major updates to their Model Context Protocol (MCP) server, introducing a fully managed remote server with OAuth authentication, dramatically improved log fetching and parsing using Apache Parquet format with smart caching, and specialized tooling for monitoring running builds. The updates address key pain points discovered after the initial release: handling massive build logs that overwhelm AI agents, eliminating local server maintenance overhead, and bridging the gap between API capabilities and practical AI agent usage. The server now enables developers to bootstrap pipelines, debug failures more efficiently, and integrate CI/CD workflows with AI tools like Claude and VS Code with minimal configuration.

recent_posts.title: Introducing Test Engine Workflows
recent_posts.summary: Buildkite Test Engine now includes workflows, a feature that automatically detects flaky tests using configurable monitors (transition count, passed on retry, probabilistic flakiness) and triggers custom actions like labeling, muting, sending notifications to Slack, or creating Linear issues. Teams can apply tag filters to monitor specific branches and create separate workflows for different test types or environments. The feature is available in public preview for Pro and Enterprise customers, with up to three workflows per suite.

recent_posts.title: Buildkite Changelog roundup: August, 2025
recent_posts.summary: Buildkite announces major platform updates including simplified Kubernetes agent setup with single token deployment, redesigned build page interface with improved navigation and search capabilities, new Pipeline Examples Gallery for easier onboarding, enhanced Test Engine features with Slack notifications and expanded framework support, and upgraded Mac hosted agents running on M4 Pro hardware delivering 30-45% faster performance for iOS builds.

recent_posts.title: Announcing Buildkite's Migration Services
recent_posts.summary: Buildkite launches Migration Services to help engineering teams transition from Jenkins, CircleCI, GitHub Actions, and other CI/CD platforms. The service offers hands-on support through a structured process including discovery calls, pipeline translation, architecture guidance, and 12 months of premium support. Teams can choose between full-service migration or guidance-only options, with the goal of optimizing performance and eliminating common CI/CD pain points like slow builds and scaling constraints.
